_why: This script is how every count in the candidate and J backlogs is produced, so a hole here is invisible in every claim derived from it -- and its worst failure was not a wrong number but a CLEAN one. Each mutation restores one way it can under-read a store, and two run the other way: the coverage guard must not fire on the file's own header prose, and the routing must not capture a candidates row that merely mentions a J-id.

mutations.name: route-the-j-registry-to-the-candidate-reader
mutations._mechanism: THE regression: `rows()` ends a row on any line starting with `|`, and skill-monitoring is full of pipe tables. Reported candidates=3 OPEN=0 for 46 real entries -- a CLEAN registry, the one answer nothing prompts you to re-check.

mutations.name: routing-ignores-the-title
mutations._mechanism: A candidates row merely MENTIONING a J-id would route to the J reader and report zero entries.
mutations.find: return any("Skill Monitoring" in ln for ln in text.split("\n")[:5])
mutations.replace: return any("Skill Monitoring" in ln for ln in text.split("\n")[:0] or ["Skill Monitoring"])

mutations.name: planned-is-not-counted-as-open
mutations._mechanism: The file's own table says MONITORING and PLANNED are the words that mean open work.

mutations.name: take-the-first-status-in-an-entry
mutations._mechanism: A census once reported J18 open because a NOTE after it contained MONITORING. Two backticked statuses is a quotation, not a verdict.
mutations.find: out.append((jid, found[0] if len(found) == 1 else None))
mutations.replace: out.append((jid, found[0] if found else None))

mutations.name: drop-the-vocabulary-diff
mutations._mechanism: L486's second missing part: a status word nobody documented is drift nobody sees.

mutations.name: drop-the-coverage-flag
mutations._mechanism: The generalisable guard. Without it an unsupported row shape reads as an empty backlog, which is exactly how this bug survived.
mutations.find: flag = "" if parsed >= present else f"   <-- {present - parsed} ROW-SHAPED LINES NOT PARSED"

mutations.name: measure-coverage-against-ids-mentioned-anywhere
mutations._mechanism: The FALSE-POSITIVE direction. Counting ids mentioned ANYWHERE puts the header's own discussion of the deliberate J31-J33 gaps into the denominator, so the guard cries wolf on the header. Coverage must be measured against a looser ROW shape, never against id mentions.
mutations.find:
loose=sum(1 for ln in text.split("\n")
                  if ln.strip().startswith("- ") and re.search(r'\*\*[A-Z]+\d+', ln))

mutations.name: print-a-candidates-total-for-a-j-registry
mutations._mechanism: `TOTAL candidates=0` for a monitoring-only run is the same false-clean shape this file now guards against.

mutations.name: severity-emoji-decides-the-status
mutations._mechanism: The leading emoji is SEVERITY; a red entry can be fixed. Inferring status from it re-invents the guess the Status: line exists to replace.
mutations.find: c=collections.Counter(s or "<none>" for _, s in entries)

mutations.name: reject-a-bold-closed-id
mutations._mechanism: Seven real entries use `**G1** —`; a regex demanding the dash immediately after the id silently drops them.

mutations.name: hardcode-j-in-the-coverage-denominator
mutations._mechanism: THE guard rigging its own baseline: filtering the missed prefixes out of the denominator reports clean while dropping 33 real rows.

mutations.name: pin-the-title-to-line-zero
mutations._mechanism: A blank first line or frontmatter routes the registry to the candidate reader and reproduces `TOTAL candidates=0` -- the exact failure this routing prevents.
mutations.find: return any("Skill Monitoring" in ln for ln in text.split("\n")[:5])
